question: Denmark has authorised Act L10 for the new Central Jutland motorway along a route that crosses major drinking-water recharge zones, despite the strict protection required under EU water legislation.

The project allows motorway construction directly above groundwater bodies where per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, de-icing salts, heavy metals and microplastics can infiltrate the water due to ineffective 50 cm edge drainage and the absence of any validated protective measures. The 50 cm edge-drainage solution is presented as protective, yet Denmark has produced no evidence demonstrating its effectiveness.

Since key obligations under the Water Framework, Groundwater and Drinking Water Directives have not been implemented, Denmark is not complying with EU law. Furthermore, the motorway is routed only 7 km from one of Northern Europe’s largest bat hibernation sites, yet it does not implement the strict protection regime required under the EU Habitats Directive for Annex IV species. 1.
Will the Commission assess whether Denmark is in breach of its EU groundwater protection obligations?
Will the Commission evaluate whether Denmark is violating its obligations under the Water Framework Directive, the Groundwater Directive and the Drinking Water Directive?
Will the Commission assess whether Act L10 breaches EU law on strict species protection?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.2.2026) Member States are responsible for carrying out all necessary environmental impact assessments of projects and ensuring that they comply with EU laws, such as water and nature rules, as well as rules on impact assessments and public consultations. More generally, Member States have primary responsibility for correctly transposing and implementing EU law.

Where a Member State fails to comply with EU law, the Commission may initiate an infringement procedure. However, the Commission’s policy regarding enforcement priorities is that, in principle, it will only initiate an infringement case if it raises general issues of principle (e.g. incorrect transposition) or where there is sufficient evidence of a general practice or of systemic shortcomings1.

The Commission therefore focuses on issues of wider impact, and not on individual cases of bad application of EU law. Moreover, the exact technical specifications of the planned L10 Central Jutland motorway are not final, and legal acts concerning the L10 motorway may still be challenged before the national courts.
1 Commission Communication of 19 January 2017 entitled “EU law: Better results through better application
(C/2016/8600, OJ C 18, 19.1.2017, p. 10–20) and Commission Communication of 13 October 2022 entitled Enforcing EU law for a Europe that delivers, COM(2022) 518 final.
